entry_state: Chapter 10 ends with purpose-specific exchangeability, the amended estimation objective and distinct initial-application adjustments. Financing, awards, EPS and consolidation all require contract rights, measurement origins, dates and reporting populations that closing totals cannot replace. The next chapter turns to credit losses and the bank balance sheet.
exit_state: The banking chapter distinguishes reported group relationships, parent cash and earnings, conditional upstream transfers, dividend declaration rules and bank-specific capital constraints. Systemic indicators need their own units, vintages and applicable rule; proposals are not operative rules. Debt carrying values, dated principal and guarantee terms answer different questions. Loan creation and expected credit loss remain to follow.
findings: Parent-only cash and consolidated restricted cash use different perimeters; their subtraction cannot establish parent unrestricted resources.
Dividend declarations, payments, earnings tests and capital-buffer payout rules use distinct dates and income definitions.
The systemic-indicator discussion keeps reporting precision, score rounding, publication dates and amendment applicability separate.
The repeated 2024 as-of date in the later note disclosure is explicitly not treated as a 2025 balance. No new confirmed defect.
